candidates: When reviewing documentation files (e.g., README.md, SKILL.md files) that contain links or references to other files in the repository, verify that each referenced filename actually exists; flag any link pointing to a non-existent file (for example, referencing `CLAUDE.local.md` when only `CLAUDE.md` exists).

Proofread prose in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` files and other Markdown documentation for incomplete sentence fragments; every explanatory sentence before a code example or sub-section must be grammatically complete.

When reviewing documentation for CLI commands (e.g., in `scripts/release/README.md`), verify that every `--option <value-list>` enumerates all values supported by the implementation; flag documented option lists that omit valid values.

In this repo, `AGENTS.md` is the canonical instruction file for all coding agents. New agent guidance must go into `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` should contain only a single `@AGENTS.md` reference line. Do not add duplicated instructions to `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or other agent entrypoints — use thin references instead.

`AGENTS.md` must contain an explicit self-maintenance directive instructing agents to update `AGENTS.md` whenever repository architecture, tooling, commands, or contributor guidance changes, and to keep `CLAUDE.md` and other agent entrypoints as thin references. Flag any PR that removes or weakens this directive.

In all Markdown files in this repository, every fenced code block must include a language specifier (e.g., ` ```bash `, ` ```text `, ` ```typescript `). Flag any code block opened with a bare ` ``` ` — this violates the MD040 markdownlint rule enforced in this codebase.

In `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` skill-body content, do not use `@<path>` file-inclusion syntax (e.g., `@.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`) to embed external files — that syntax is only valid in root-level agent entry files such as `CLAUDE.md`. Within a skill body, reference files with a standard Markdown link or inline the relevant content directly.

In skill files that present a list of labels or options for agents to choose from, each option must include a specific, actionable condition explaining when to select it — a short noun phrase is insufficient. For example, a CI label entry should state exact triggering conditions (e.g., 'use `ci:daily` when changes affect prerelease sandboxes or sandboxes pinned to a non-latest framework or React version') rather than just a name.

`.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` files that describe workflows primarily useful outside the monorepo (e.g., upgrading Storybook in an external app, QA-testing a canary build in a downstream project) must include an explicit section explaining the skill's relevance and typical usage context for monorepo contributors.

In `AGENTS.md`, command examples for routine agent tasks (compilation, type-checking, linting, testing) should default to the faster non-production variants; do not include `-c production` or `--no-link` as the default. Reserve those flags for explicitly labeled 'CI-parity' or 'sandbox-related' sections, with a note explaining when they are required.

`AGENTS.md` should include a concise scenario-based command reference — ideally a table mapping common tasks to exact commands (e.g., 'Compile one package → `yarn nx compile <package-name>`'). Pure prose descriptions of the build system are insufficient; agents need a quick-reference lookup of the most common development scenarios.

When documenting commands in `AGENTS.md` that accept a file-path argument, are run from the repository root, but operate on files inside a subdirectory (e.g., `code/`), explicitly state what the path is relative to and prefer the `--cwd` form where available (e.g., `yarn --cwd code lint:js:cmd <file-relative-to-code-folder> --fix`) to prevent agents from constructing incorrect paths.

Keep `AGENTS.md` focused on information agents actively need to make decisions or run commands. Remove or omit sections that are purely informational for humans but do not guide agent behavior (e.g., a bare table of environment variable names with no instruction on when an agent should set them); excess content increases token cost without improving agent output.
